newsitem.title: USA: U.S. crude oil leads energy prices lower on ACCESS.
newsitem.headline: U.S. crude oil leads energy prices lower on ACCESS.

text.p: U.S. crude oil prices led the energy complex lower early in after-hours trade, as players continued to take profits after a day of sharp declines on NYMEX.
Data from the American Petroleum Institute (API) and U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA) showed a 1.3 million barrel rise in distillates held in primary storage last week.
"It's an excuse to take profits," one ACCESS after-hours trader said.
After hours, NYMEX crude oil took 17 cents off its settlement of $25.07 a barrel. A total of 610 lots traded early into ACCESS.
The contract lost 47 cents a barrel on the day.
Traders saw crude leading the complex further into negative territory on Thursday, with support seen $24.75.
"We're not too far away from it now," the trader said, adding the next key technical level was $24.10.
Gasoline followed crude down, breaking a recent low by touching 65.10 cents a gallon after-hours.
Traders said if unleaded fell under 65.10 in the daytime session, the next support level was 64.20 cents.
Front-month gasoline traded 65.25 cents on a light 26 lots in all months.
Heating oil traded 73.60 cents a gallon after-hours, after sliding by 2.22 cents during the day session and falling another 0.33 cent on ACCESS. About 326 lots changed hands.
